content.text: The demo page confirmed Physics2DPlugin is the plugin used, but the demo is about projectile/particle motion (gravity/velocity/angle), which isn't ideal for a button click feedback (no projectile launch). For Like/Save/Share buttons we want a tactile rebound — that's CustomBounce + CustomEase territory. I'll provide a precise answer based on the canonical physics-based button feedback pattern and note what the demo actually demonstrates.

input.title: Create physics-based effects
input.technique: Physics2DPlugin for projectile motion (gravity + velocity + angle + friction). The demo itself is a particle/projectile launcher — not directly a button click micro-interaction. The transferable idea for Like/Save/Share is the broader GSAP "physics-based effects" toolkit: Physics2DPlugin for confetti/particle bursts on tap, plus CustomBounce + CustomEase for the tactile button rebound itself. The recommended port combines both: a CustomBounce squish-and-rebound on the button transform, layered with an optional Physics2D particle burst on tap (great for Like), and a per-button CSS-variable color flash driven by the same timeline.
input.keyMechanic: Physics2DPlugin animates `physics2D: { velocity, angle, gravity, friction }` on each tick — it integrates position from velocity/gravity rather than tweening to a fixed endpoint, which is what makes it feel "real". For the button feedback, you (a) overshoot the scale with CustomBounce.create("myBounce", { strength: 0.6, endAtStart: true, squash: 2 }) so the button squishes, snaps back, and settles, (b) flash a per-element CSS variable (--flash-color) to that button's brand color using gsap.fromTo on the variable so it's keyframed, and (c) optionally spawn N short-lived particle divs and animate each with `physics2D` for a confetti burst (Like only). All three are merged into one gsap.timeline() so the tactile feel, color flash, and burst stay in lockstep.
input.a11yNotes: - The feedback is purely additive: the React onClick still fires synchronously, so screen reader / keyboard users get identical behavior. The timeline is fire-and-forget. - Wrap the entire effect in `if (!gsap.matchMedia().reduced) { ... }` or check `window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` and, when true, skip the squish/burst and just toggle `--flash-alpha` to 0.6 for 120ms via a single non-bouncy tween — color feedback remains, motion does not. - Particles get `pointer-events:none` and are removed onComplete so they never trap focus or block taps. - Use `transform-origin: 50% 60%` so the rebound visually anchors at the thumb, which reads as more "tactile" without affecting hit-target geometry. - Color choice for Like (#ff3860) and Save (#d4a24a) should be checked against the reading-view background for 3:1 non-text contrast (WCAG 1.4.11); the blurred glow alone is decorative, but if it's the only feedback in reduced-motion mode it must meet contrast. - Buttons keep their `:focus-visible` ring untouched — the ::after layer sits behind (z-index: -1) so it never masks the focus outline. - For the Like burst, particles are fixed-position but absolute-removed onComplete; they will not affect document flow, layout shift (CLS), or assistive-tech tree (they're empty spans).
